title: wksplit-cs-utility (ref): incidents + dated lessons
desc: T3 reference tier: wkhippo incident post-mortem, the cheap-models-drop-code failure class, and the 6-gate hardening origin. Read when diagnosing a regression or extending the splitter. Parent: wksplit-cs-utility. Howto: wksplit-cs-utility-howto.
steps: WKHIPPO INCIDENT (2026-06-10): A Flash-generated PS split of wkfind.ps1 moved param() below module dot-sourcing. param() is not the first statement -> PowerShell treats it as a command call -> 'param not recognized' error. Symptom: script PARSES CLEAN via [Parser]::ParseFile (no syntax error) but dies on first runtime execution. Root cause: param-displacement (G1 PARAM-FIRST gate did not exist yet). Recovery: git checkout of the pre-split monolith.

DROPPED FUNCTIONS (wkhippo root cause 2): Same Flash split silently dropped Get-Tokens and Invoke-CheckedScript. Mechanism: the splitter extracted functions into modules but omitted two; no syntax error because PowerShell's AST parse does not verify CommandAst names. Result: CommandNotFoundException at runtime. Root cause: no SYMBOL-REFERENCE PRE-CHECK existed (G3 gate did not exist yet). Lesson: a parse-clean split can be functionally dead. G3 gate = collect all DEFINED functions across all planned modules via FunctionDefinitionAst, compare to all CALLED names via CommandAst.GetCommandName(); any called name that is defined in the ORIGINAL but missing from the planned output is a DROPPED function -> auto-remerge or FAIL.

CHEAP-MODELS-DROP-CODE CLASS (2026-06-05): Haiku agent was used for a source split; silently dropped ~320 lines of critical SuggestCommand.Resolve logic. Code compiled, tests passed, functionality broken. Root cause: Haiku deems long conditional blocks 'boilerplate' and omits them. Class applies to all cheap models on long files. Rule: do NOT use Haiku (or codex-mini without verification) for source splits. Use the deterministic tool or Opus.

G2 REGEX-HOIST ORIGIN (2026-06-10): wkfind.ps1 contained Korean Hangul chars in inline regex literals. After split + bash->PowerShell relay the non-ASCII bytes became garbled, triggering ArgumentException on first regex use. Root: non-ASCII regex literals are encoding-fragile across relay paths. Fix: REGEX-HOIST gate converts each non-ASCII inline literal to a :<Name>Rx var using \uXXXX escapes, placed after param(). QA-canary (Haiku) surfaced this by actually running the tool and hitting the ArgumentException, demonstrating the 'run-verify is mandatory' lesson.

G5 COMPILE-LOOP ORIGIN (2026-06-10): Early splitter versions would exit after writing files even if dotnet build failed. Operators would then manually repair broken splits. Hardened: splitter must run dotnet build in a loop, auto-remerge any member causing CS0103/CS0246, retry until 0 errors AND 0 warnings. Exit only on clean build. This makes shipping a broken C# split structurally impossible.

G6 SELFTEST CS0111 TRAP (2026-06-11): During G6 selftest, the original .cs file was copied into the temp project dir alongside the split partials. Both define the same types -> CS0111 duplicate member. The G5 compile loop must not treat CS0111 as auto-correctable (it is unrecoverable without removing a file). Fix: rename the original backup to .bak (non-.cs extension) before compiling partials in the temp dir.

ALLMAN-BRACE BUG (2026-06-11): wksplit-cs.py was only tested on inline-brace style (class Foo {). When brace is on its own line (allman: class Foo\n{), three bugs fired: (a) make_header did not emit { so partial files had no class body start; (b) class_body_start() double-emitted the { line; (c) find_members() detected class indent from a blank line (indent=0), skipping all members. Fixed by: (a) always emit { in make_header; (b) skip the { line in content iterator; (c) detect indent from first NON-BLANK line at start_idx.
